regime_context: TSX detector shows Big Banks as the current regime leader (rank 2, but the only high-score theme that is trend-gated eligible with durability 0.80), while Oil & Gas holds the highest raw momentum score yet is NOT eligible (durability 0.19, mixed hurst) — a leadership handoff toward banks is forming but not confirmed. Breadth of rotation is narrowing (44% of themes eligible), momentum rank-IC is ~0 (focus lens only), and the macro flow is dominated by AI/tech headlines with 100% unscheduled surprises, so this is a market where trend discipline helps on drawdown but direction is highly uncertain; past desk directional accuracy is weak (0.313 over 147 graded calls), so lean low.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Gold Miners (durability 0.56, mixed hurst, breath 0.5, score 0.39, eligible) can lift durability above ~0.7 AND flip hurst to 'trend' while maintaining eligibility — if BOTH occur and breadth expands above 0.7, I would retire this watch and re-grade it as a low-conviction overweight candidate. Until then it stays a non-call.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only theme combining trend-gate eligibility with high durability (0.80), a clean trend hurst tag, full breadth (1.0), and no crowding flag — the strongest staying-power profile in a narrowing rotation. Momentum ranks as a focus lens, but the combination of eligible + durable + broad + uncrowded is exactly what the validated absolute-trend gate rewards for drawdown control.
theses.dissent: Banks at 0.99 score are actually second to Oil & Gas at 1.215; if Oil & Gas regains eligibility (durability repairs), capital may rotate back and banks become a crowded beta trade. The rotation margin is only 0.225 — narrow enough to flip without warning.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO lags the S&P/TSX composite by 5% or more over any rolling 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Staples screens well on trend (durability 0.79, hurst trend, breadth 1.0, eligible) but carries a crowding flag (crowding_z 1.03, crowded == true). Crowding is a size-down caution only — never a short — and with banks offering a similar defensive/trend profile without the crowding, there is little marginal reason to hold this over banks.
evidence: crowded == true (crowding_z 1.03) — the only eligible, crowded trend theme
banks offer comparable profile with crowding_z 0.61 and no crowding flag
theses.dissent: Crowding flags have no basket-level forward edge and mark tops only in per-name extension — this could simply be a strongly owned, steady uptrend with continued inflows. Avoiding it concedes a high-durability trend leg.

falsifier.text: XST.TO outperforms ZEB.TO by 5% or more over any rolling 15-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas has the top momentum score (1.215, rank 1) but is NOT trend-gate eligible, with a low durability bar (0.19) and mixed hurst tag — the exact pattern the validated gate exists to screen out. The rotation headline shows it as the current 'leader' with the weakest durability of any top-ranked theme, meaning its leadership is fragile even if the score looks dominant.
theses.dissent: Raw momentum is strongest here and energy is a headline macro theme; if the durability bar repairs quickly, this becomes the cleanest trend buy in the TSX. Avoiding it risks missing the strongest near-term impulse.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO achieves trend-gate eligibility (durability bar above ~0.5 and trend hurst) and sustains outperformance vs ZEB.TO over 10 days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
